To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the timestamps used to timestamp database states must agree with a transaction serialization order; and (2) a database can delay the choice of timestamps until a serialization order is determined, reducing the chance of aborted transactions, and also providing timestamps that are more consistent with a serialization ordering.

we have devised a timestamping scheme that: (1) is consistent with the SQL-2 standard; (2) is compatible with the two-phase locking concurrency-control protocol, (3) can avoid aborting transactions that would otherwise be aborted, (4) can detect read-write conflicts, which are necessary to establish a serialization order.
we provide a simple and effective method to timestamp records in a transaction time database, such that the timestamps are consistent with a commit order.
